segments: ... Ilghazi {OCR?} son of Artuq, lord of Mardin,
and in his place arose Husam al-Din Yuluq Arslan;
and he was a young boy.
Because Zahir al-Din Shah-Arman was the maternal uncle of the boy,
he appointed as his administrator one of his father's slaves named Nizam al-Din.
And this Nizam al-Din took the mother of the boy as a wife,
and administered the kingdom well.
Then that youth Husam al-Din died,
and he had a brother who was younger than he,
whose name was Qutb al-Din, after the name of his father;
and Nizam al-Din placed him in his brother's place.
While the boy possessed only the title,
the entire administration belonged to Nizam al-Din and his slave Lu'lu'.
And when that boy grew up,
and saw that he was ruler in name and not in deed,
he went in to Nizam al-Din one day when he was sick,
that is to say, to visit him.
And as he was leaving,
Lu'lu' went out with him as far as the gate,
as if to honor him.
And when they reached a narrow place,
Qutb al-Din struck Lu'lu' with a knife and killed him.
And he returned to Nizam al-Din while he was lying in his bed,
and killed him too.
And he took the heads of both of them,
and threw them down from the fortress to the nobles.
And when they saw,
they were all afraid of him,
and they submitted to him.
Now this murder was carried out in the year six hundred and one of the Arabs (1204/5 AD),
twenty years after Nizam al-Din took power.
And in the year 578 (1182 AD),
or 579 of the Arabs,
Salah al-Din went to Aleppo.
And from there he crossed the Euphrates,
and took Edessa from Muzaffar al-Din son of Zayn al-Din, its lord.
And he went to Resh'ayna (Ra's al-'Ayn),
and from there to Dara.
And 'Imad al-Din son of Qara Arslan came to him,
in place of his brother Nur al-Din, who was ill and unable to come.
And from there he came to the city of Balad,
and went and encamped against Mosul.
And there also came to him the lord of Erbil, Zayn al-Din son of 'Ali Kuchak;
and his brother Muzaffar al-Din, lord of Harran, was also with Salah al-Din.
And Salah al-Din pressed Mosul with a siege.
And the mother of 'Izz al-Din, lord of Mosul, came out to him—
she who was the daughter of Artuq—
